title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (Longue Marche continuation, ms. pp. 721-722). X = U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,∞}. Its generalized Jacobian is the split rank-2 torus T^0 = J^0 = G_m^{{0,1,∞}}/diag. S_3 acts on X, on the three cusps, and hence on T^0. Grothendieck wants a canonical, S_3-equivariant Abel-Jacobi map U_{0,3,S} → T^0_S over an arbitrary base S. The obstruction and uniqueness questions are H^1 and H^0 of S_3-equivariant cohomology H^*(S, S_3; T^0).

On the previous page he computed H^0(Spec Z, S_3; J^0) = 1 using the description ker(G_m^3 → G_m) with x0x1x∞ = 1. There the invariants are the cube roots of unity in Z, hence trivial.

On this page he takes the Hochschild-Serre / Grothendieck spectral sequence for a finite group acting on a sheaf over a base with trivial action:
E_2^{pq} = H^p(S_3, H^q(S, J^0)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(S, S_3; J^0).
Its low-degree exact sequence is
0 → H^1(S_3, H^0(S,J^0)) → H^1(S, S_3; J^0) → H^0(S_3, H^1(S,J^0)) → H^2(S_3, H^0(S,J^0)).
For S_0 = Spec Z, H^1(S_0, J^0) = Pic(Z)^2 = 0, so H^1 equivariant equals H^1(S_3, J^0(Z)).

He then notes this is unnecessary. Write J^0(S) = M_A ⊗ I with I = G_m(S), and H^1(S, J^0) = M_A ⊗ Pic(S). Here M_A is the cocharacter lattice Z^3/Z(1,1,1), equivalently the sign-twisted kernel lattice. A general lemma (309) states H^0(S_3, M_A⊗I) = H^1(S_3, M_A⊗I) = 0 for every abelian group I with trivial action.

Check of (309): use 0 → I → I^3 = Ind_{S_2}^{S_3} I → I^3/I → 0. By Shapiro, H^k(S_3, I^3) = H^k(S_2, I). Restriction S_2 → S_3 induces an isomorphism on H^0 and H^1 (both Hom(Z/2, I)). It is also an isomorphism on H^2 = Ext(Z/2, I) = I/2, since H_2(S_3) = 0. The long exact sequence then gives H^0 = H^1 = 0.

Hence (310): H^0(S, S_3; T^0) = H^1(S, S_3; T^0) = 0 for every scheme S. On the next page this becomes the Proposition: every (S_3, T^0)-torsor has a unique S_3-invariant section. The Corollary follows: there is a unique S_3-equivariant morphism φ: U_{0,3,S} → T^0_S inducing the identity on the generalized Jacobian. Concretely it is the line x0+x1+x∞ = 0 in G_m^3/G_m, i.e. P^1 as a line in P^2 minus the coordinate triangle.
errors: (310) as written reads 'H^0(S_3, S_3; J^0) ≃ H^1(S, S_3, J^0) = 0'. The first argument should be the base S, and the intended statement is H^0 = H^1 = 0 (both vanish), not an isomorphism.

Subtlety in the previous page's description. With the plain permutation action, the two tori G_m^3/diag and ker(G_m^3 → G_m) are not S_3-equivariantly isomorphic; they differ by a sign twist, as the margin note 'attention ... à un signe près' records. For ker(product) with permutation action, H^0(S, S_3; ·) = μ_3(S), which is nonzero e.g. over Z[ζ_3]. The x^3 = 1 computation on p.721 is therefore special to S = Spec Z. The general statement (309)/(310) is correct only for T^0 = G_m^3/diag, equivalently the sign-twisted kernel, which is what M_A encodes.
Minor: the step reducing to H^1(S_0,J^0) = Pic(S_0)^2 assumes T^0 split of rank 2, which holds. As his marginal NB says, it is superseded by (309) applied to I = Pic(S).

ideas.what: Spectral sequence H^p(G, H^q(S,F)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(S, G; F) for equivariant cohomology with a finite group acting on the coefficients
ideas.modern_name: Hochschild-Serre / Grothendieck spectral sequence for equivariant (G-sheaf) cohomology

ideas.what: H^0 = H^1 = 0 for S_3 acting on (Z^3/Z)⊗I, for any trivial module I
ideas.modern_name: Group cohomology of the A_2 (co)weight lattice via Shapiro's lemma

ideas.what: Unique rigidification of (S_3, T^0)-torsors; canonical S_3-equivariant Abel-Jacobi embedding of P^1-{0,1,∞} into its generalized Jacobian G_m^3/G_m over any base, image the line x0+x1+x∞ = 0
ideas.modern_name: Equivariant Albanese/Abel-Jacobi map for U_{0,3}; generalized Jacobian (Rosenlicht-Serre)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Rosenlicht/Serre for generalized Jacobians; the line model is classical
ideas.where_published: Part of the unpublished continuation of La Longue Marche (pp. 650bis-787)

missed.claim: Careful treatment of the sign twist distinguishing the S_3-tori G_m^3/diag and ker(G_m^3 → G_m). Equivariant rigidity holds over every base for the former but fails for the latter, whose equivariant H^0 is μ_3. This is a small technical point in the unpublished Longue Marche continuation, not a new result.
missed.quote: (310) H^0(S, S_3; J^0) = H^1(S, S_3, J^0) = 0 pour tout schéma S
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's normalization of the S_3-equivariant Abel-Jacobi map for P^1-{0,1,∞} over Spec Z, relevant to rigidifications in the Teichmüller-tower program. The mathematics is elementary and standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine equivariant-cohomology computation (Hochschild-Serre plus Shapiro) yielding unique rigidification of S_3-equivariant T^0-torsors. Correct and neatly done, but nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: 'les calculs faits plus [?] ailleurs' should read 'les calculs faits par ailleurs montrent que'.
(310) should read 'H^0(S, S_3; J^0) = H^1(S, S_3; J^0) = 0'. The first slot has an overwritten/struck symbol replaced by S.
The bracketed '(Z^*)^{0,1,∞}/Z^* ≃ Z^*⊗_Z M_0' under H^0(S_0, J^0) is crossed out in the manuscript.
In the E_2 term, H^q(S_0, J^0) is underlined (H̲^q), and E_2^{pq} is written above it.
Margin NB reads: 'on n'a pas besoin de la relation Pic(S)=0'.
